name: Maintain and repair laboratory instruments
summary: Laboratory analysers and general equipment need repairs when they fail and scheduled maintenance and calibration to stay accurate. Technologists troubleshoot faults first and call the manufacturer's support line, biomedical technicians coordinate vendor field engineers, keep the maintenance log and service general equipment themselves, and an instrument returns to patient testing only after calibration and QC pass and a charge technologist signs it off. Most elapsed time is waiting for the vendor's engineer or parts and for scheduled visit dates, while the instrument's work moves to backup analysers.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community and reference laboratory company with nine laboratories, automated analyser lines under vendor service contracts and a small biomedical engineering team.
baseline.notes: Daily and weekly operator maintenance is part of the testing and daily QC processes and is not counted as an event here; monthly and quarterly operator maintenance is.

trigger: The laboratory logs a fault, a scheduled maintenance or calibration task comes due, or the vendor schedules a preventive maintenance visit or field action.
end_state: The equipment is back in service with calibration, QC and the maintenance record complete, or it is retired.

volume.seasonality: Fairly even; vendor preventive maintenance clusters around service contract schedules and fewer visits are booked in late December.

evidence.note: Volume from the organisation file's process map; the mix of faults (42 per cent), vendor maintenance (20 per cent), in-house maintenance of general equipment (25 per cent) and periodic operator maintenance (13 per cent) is the author's estimate.

Equipment control program in the company's QMS (dyn_lic); duties from the occupation description (wiki_bmet). FTE on this process is the author's estimate within the six technicians, who also handle equipment purchases, installations and validations.

roles.title: Medical laboratory technologist, chemistry and haematology

evidence.note: Routine maintenance and QC by technologists (job_mlt); FTE is an estimate of time on troubleshooting, vendor calls, periodic maintenance and post-repair QC; reference and toxicology technologists do the same work in their laboratories.

roles.title: Charge technologist
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Coordinates troubleshooting, service and repair and signs maintenance sheets (job_charge); FTE is an estimate.

roles.title: Laboratory manager (discipline)
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Approves non-contract repair quotes and replacement requests; estimate.

systems.name: Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Instrument middleware with autoverification and rerun rules
Quality control data management software (rules, peer comparison)
Quality management system software (document control, CAPA, training records)
ERP for general ledger, payables, procurement and inventory
Automated chemistry and immunoassay analysers on track lines
Haematology analysers, slide makers and coagulation analysers

steps.name: Open the work order in the maintenance log
steps.description: A maintenance request logged by the laboratory after a fault, a preventive maintenance task coming due in the CMMS or a vendor's scheduled visit or field notice creates a work order with the instrument's asset number, location and type of event.
inputs: maintenance request, due PM task or vendor notice

error.defect_description: Work order opened against the wrong asset.

next.condition: vendor preventive maintenance or field action
in-house scheduled maintenance or calibration of general equipment
periodic operator maintenance on an analyser

evidence.note: Equipment program and CMMS described (dyn_lic, wiki_cmms); the event mix is the author's estimate for about 550 events a month across nine laboratories.

steps.name: Troubleshoot the fault at the bench
steps.description: The technologist reads the instrument's error codes and logs, follows the operator manual's troubleshooting steps (clean or replace the probe, tubing or lamp, reseat a module, restart), runs the function checks and decides whether the operator fix worked.

error.defect_description: Wrong cause assumed, so the fault recurs.

next.condition: general equipment the biomedical technician repairs

evidence.note: Troubleshooting and routine maintenance by technologists (job_charge, job_mlt); causes checked during recovery (clp_c24). Share fixed by the operator is an estimate.

steps.name: Call the vendor's technical support and troubleshoot remotely
steps.description: The technologist calls the manufacturer's support line with the serial number and error codes, waits for a callback, follows the specialist's instructions or lets the specialist connect remotely, and learns whether an engineer must come on site.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: part shipped for the operator to fit

evidence.note: Vendor phone and remote support before dispatch is common practice for laboratory analysers; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Log the service call and arrange the engineer's visit
steps.description: The biomedical technician records the vendor's case number in the CMMS, checks whether the instrument is under a service contract, arranges building access and confirms the visit time with the charge technologist.

error.defect_description: Visit booked without checking contract coverage, so an unplanned invoice follows.

evidence.note: Coordinating service and repair (job_charge) and working with manufacturers' field engineers (wiki_bmet); contract share is an estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the field engineer or parts
steps.description: The instrument stays out of service while the vendor's field engineer travels to the laboratory, usually within the contract's response time, or while a part ships; work moves to a backup analyser or a sister laboratory.
outputs: engineer on site or part received

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Next-business-day on-site response is typical of analyser service contracts; no contract text was opened, so the range is an estimate.

steps.name: Field engineer repairs the instrument
steps.description: The vendor's field service engineer diagnoses the fault, replaces parts, adjusts and tests the instrument and leaves a service report; the time shown is the repair's duration, during which laboratory staff are not needed.

error.defect_description: Repair incomplete, so the fault returns within days.

next.condition: needs another part or a second visit

evidence.note: Field service engineers repair equipment (wiki_bmet); duration and repeat-visit share are estimates.

steps.name: Review the service report and update the CMMS
steps.description: The biomedical technician reads the engineer's service report, records parts replaced, labour and downtime in the CMMS, flags major maintenance that requires calibration verification, files the report and passes any non-contract invoice to accounts payable.

error.defect_description: Major maintenance not flagged, so calibration verification is skipped.

evidence.note: Maintenance history in the CMMS (wiki_cmms); major maintenance triggers calibration verification (cfr1255). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Repair general laboratory equipment in-house
steps.description: The biomedical technician repairs centrifuges, refrigerators and freezers, incubators, water baths, pipettes and similar equipment, replacing parts from stock or ordering them, and decides whether the item can be repaired at all.

error.defect_description: Repair not verified, so the equipment fails again.

evidence.note: Biomedical technicians repair and calibrate laboratory equipment (wiki_bmet); shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Calibrate and run QC after the repair or maintenance
steps.description: The technologist recalibrates the affected assays, runs calibration verification after major maintenance, runs all QC levels and evaluates them against the multirule limits in the QC software before asking for release.

error.defect_description: A marginal shift accepted.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation: equipment returned to service only after calibration and QC are acceptable, calibration verification after major maintenance (equivalent to 42 CFR 493.1255), Westgard multirule acceptance

evidence.note: Calibration verification after major maintenance (cfr1255); resume testing only when QC is acceptable (clp_c24); multirule acceptance (westgard). Failure share is an estimate.

steps.name: Charge technologist reviews and returns the instrument to service
steps.description: The charge technologist reviews the maintenance record, calibration and QC, signs the maintenance sheet, removes the out-of-service tag, turns autoverification back on in the middleware and tells the bench and, if needed, client services that normal testing has resumed.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation: equipment returned to service only after calibration and QC are acceptable, calibration verification after major maintenance (equivalent to 42 CFR 493.1255), Westgard multirule acceptance

evidence.note: Signing maintenance sheets and acting on QC (job_charge); autoverification is switched off during an out-of-control event (clp_c24).

steps.name: Verify performance after in-house repair or maintenance
steps.description: The biomedical technician checks that the equipment meets its specification before use: centrifuge speed and timer with a tachometer, refrigerator and freezer temperatures against a reference thermometer, pipette volumes by weighing, and records the readings.

error.defect_description: Out-of-tolerance reading accepted.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation equipment requirements: maintenance and function checks per the manufacturer, documented, before patient testing (equivalent to 42 CFR 493.1254)

evidence.note: Function checks within limits before patient testing (cfr1254); calibration by biomedical technicians (wiki_bmet).

steps.name: Schedule the vendor's preventive maintenance visit
steps.description: The biomedical technician agrees the date of the vendor's preventive maintenance or software update with the charge technologist, choosing low-volume hours, arranging a backup analyser and confirming the engineer's visit.
inputs: vendor PM schedule or field notice

error.defect_description: Visit booked during a peak run, delaying results.

evidence.note: Maintenance at the manufacturer's frequency (cfr1254); coordinating service with the section (job_charge). Scheduling lead time is an estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the scheduled vendor visit
steps.description: The visit date is set by the vendor's engineer roster and the laboratory's quiet periods, so the work order waits for the agreed day.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Lead time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Vendor engineer performs the preventive maintenance
steps.description: The field engineer replaces wear parts, cleans and adjusts modules, installs software updates and runs the manufacturer's checks, leaving a service report; the time shown is the visit's duration.

error.defect_description: Part fitted incorrectly, causing a later fault.

evidence.note: Manufacturer-defined preventive maintenance (cfr1254) by field service engineers (wiki_bmet); duration is an estimate.

steps.name: Perform scheduled in-house maintenance or calibration
steps.description: When the CMMS lists a task as due, the biomedical technician services general equipment (centrifuges, refrigerators, incubators, biosafety cabinet coordination, balances, pipettes, temperature recorders), checks its performance and decides whether it passes.

error.defect_description: Task signed off without all checks.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation equipment requirements: maintenance and function checks per the manufacturer, documented, before patient testing (equivalent to 42 CFR 493.1254)

evidence.note: Equipment program covers maintenance and calibration (dyn_lic); laboratory-defined protocols where no manufacturer protocol exists (cfr1254). Times and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Close the work order and file the maintenance record
steps.description: The biomedical technician completes the CMMS record with labour, parts, downtime and results, attaches the signed sheets, sets the next due date and makes the record available to the laboratory's QC and accreditation files.

error.defect_description: Record incomplete, found at an accreditation inspection.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation equipment requirements: maintenance and function checks per the manufacturer, documented, before patient testing (equivalent to 42 CFR 493.1254); records kept for accreditation inspection

evidence.note: Documented maintenance (cfr1254) in the CMMS (wiki_cmms) under the equipment program (dyn_lic); times are estimates.

steps.name: Recommend retirement and replacement of the equipment
steps.description: For equipment beyond economic repair or no longer supported by the vendor, the biomedical technician documents the repair history and cost, tags the item out of use and drafts a replacement request with a quote.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Decommissioning is part of the equipment program (dyn_lic); repair-versus-replace cost comparison from the CMMS (wiki_cmms).

steps.name: Laboratory manager approves the retirement and replacement
steps.description: The laboratory manager reviews the request against the capital budget, approves the purchase or a loaner, and the item is decommissioned in the CMMS; validation of the replacement is a separate project.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Capital spending authority and equipment decommissioning procedure in the QMS

evidence.note: Approval authority and timing are estimates.

steps.name: Perform periodic operator maintenance on the analyser
steps.description: The technologist does the monthly or quarterly maintenance the manufacturer assigns to operators (replacing lamps, filters, seals or probes, deep-cleaning modules, running maintenance programs), records it on the maintenance sheet and runs the checks the manual requires.

error.defect_description: Step missed or part seated badly, causing a fault or QC shift.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation equipment requirements: maintenance and function checks per the manufacturer, documented, before patient testing (equivalent to 42 CFR 493.1254)

evidence.note: Technologists perform routine maintenance (job_mlt) at the manufacturer's frequency (cfr1254); times are estimates.

steps.name: Laboratory manager approves a non-contract repair quote
steps.description: For instruments without a service contract the vendor sends a quote for the visit and parts; the laboratory manager approves it and a purchase order is raised before the engineer is dispatched.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Purchasing authority: manager approval and purchase order before non-contract service

evidence.note: Common purchasing control; timing is an estimate.

exceptions.name: Vendor engineer needed
exceptions.description: The operator and the vendor's phone support cannot fix the fault, so an engineer is dispatched and the instrument waits out of service.

exceptions.name: Repeat visit for parts
exceptions.description: The engineer needs a part that is not in the van or a second visit.

exceptions.name: QC fails after repair
exceptions.description: Calibration or QC is still unacceptable after the repair, so troubleshooting starts again.

exceptions.name: Non-contract repair
exceptions.description: The instrument is not under a service contract, so a quote and manager approval come before the visit.

exceptions.name: Retirement
exceptions.description: General equipment beyond economic repair is decommissioned and a replacement requested.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from work order to return to service or retirement
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for this company's event mix

evidence.note: No published benchmark was opened. Operator and remote fixes return the instrument the same or next day, vendor dispatches typically take one to three days, in-house scheduled tasks are done within a few days of falling due and scheduled vendor visits take one to two weeks from scheduling; closing the record adds up to a day or two.

benchmarks.population: US CLIA rule followed by CAP-accredited laboratories

pain_points.description: An instrument waits out of service for the vendor's engineer or parts, and its work moves to backup analysers or sister laboratories, delaying results.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: Technologists spend bench time on phone troubleshooting with vendor support before an engineer is sent.

evidence.note: Coordinating troubleshooting, service and repair is part of the charge technologist role.

pain_points.description: After every significant repair the analyser needs recalibration, calibration verification and QC before it can be released, and a failed QC sends the work back to troubleshooting.
Service reports and maintenance sheets are re-keyed into the CMMS and filed for accreditation, and missing records surface only at inspections.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

sources.title: Licences and quality commitment
sources.supports: The quality management system includes equipment control programs that cover inventory, validation, maintenance, calibration and decommissioning; laboratories hold ISO 15189, CAP, ISO/IEC 17025, SAMHSA and MANQAP accreditations and provincial licences.

sources.title: Charge Technologist Chemistry, Winnipeg (job posting #2025-10930)
sources.supports: Ensures routine equipment maintenance is performed; coordinates troubleshooting, maintenance, service and/or repair of section equipment when staff request it; ensures QC checks are run and reviewed and acts when QC fails; signs maintenance sheets; knowledge of CAP program requirements; first point of contact for operational issues.

sources.title: Medical Laboratory Technologist, Haematology, Winnipeg (job posting #2026-12153)
sources.supports: Sets up and adjusts laboratory equipment; ensures QC checks are run and reviewed; performs routine maintenance of laboratory equipment; evening and Saturday shifts.

sources.title: 42 CFR 493.1254 Standard: Maintenance and function checks
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Maintenance as defined by the manufacturer and at least as often as specified; function checks within the manufacturer's limits before patient testing; laboratories document maintenance and function checks and set their own protocols where no manufacturer protocol exists. US rule used as a documented analogue; CAP accreditation applies equivalent requirements.

sources.title: 42 CFR 493.1255 Standard: Calibration and calibration verification procedures
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Calibration verification at least every 6 months and after major preventive maintenance or replacement of critical parts that may influence test performance, after complete reagent changes and when controls show unresolved shifts; calibration and verification must be documented.

sources.title: The 7 best practices to recover from an out-of-control event
sources.supports: Based on CLSI C24: stop reporting and turn off autoverification for the affected assay, reroute samples to an instrument with acceptable QC, investigate calibration, reagent and maintenance causes, resume patient testing only when QC meets acceptance criteria, re-analyse earlier samples and document every step.

sources.title: Westgard Rules: multirule QC
sources.supports: Multirule QC: 1-2s warning; 1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 4-1s and 10x rejection rules; a run is rejected if any rejection rule is violated.

sources.title: Biomedical equipment technician
sources.supports: Biomedical equipment technicians install, inspect, maintain, repair and calibrate equipment, some specialising in laboratory equipment; manufacturers' field service engineers support service; equipment management needs recorded documentation of how equipment was maintained and tested.

sources.title: Computerized maintenance management system
sources.supports: A CMMS keeps a database of maintenance operations, tracks assigned and completed tasks, identifies which machines need maintenance and which spare parts are stocked, and its data can verify regulatory compliance.

assumptions: One case is one work order. Daily and weekly operator maintenance is part of the testing and daily QC workflows and is excluded; monthly and quarterly operator maintenance, vendor preventive maintenance, in-house maintenance and calibration of general equipment, and repairs are included.

The organisation file lists only testing processes and the vendor as triggers. Scheduled in-house maintenance of a laboratory's equipment is counted under the testing process that owns it, and vendor-scheduled maintenance and field actions under the vendor.

Shared technologist steps use the core laboratory technologist role (mlt_core); reference and toxicology technologists do the same work in their laboratories. The core and reference testing workflows already include the hands-on time to hold specimens, log the fault and rerun samples after repair, so that time is not repeated here.

US CLIA rules (42 CFR 493.1254 and 493.1255) are used as the documented description of maintenance and calibration requirements that CAP accreditation applies; the ISO 15189 and Accreditation Canada texts were not opened.
Vendor response and repair times, the event mix and the branch shares are the author's estimates; no service contract or downtime study was opened because web search capacity ran out.
Vendor engineers' work is shown as wait time on external steps because it costs the company contract or invoice money, not staff time.
The lab manager role approves non-contract repairs and replacements; it is in the organisation file but not in this process's role list there.
Loaded costs are from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
